fields.v: Zhang, Z., Xu, Y., Liang, J., Li, W., Chen, X., Qian, L., Pei, X., Huang, J., Sun, R., Wu, Y. (2026). RepoZero: Can LLMs Generate a Code Repository from Scratch? 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Track on Evaluations and Datasets. Read from arXiv:2605.07122v3 [cs.SE], 20 May 2026. Code: https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/RepoZero
Conference — NeurIPS 2026, Track on Evaluations and Datasets (footer of the paper); full text read from arXiv:2605.07122v3

Peking University, China (Zhang, Xu, Wu); Baidu Inc, China (Liang, Li, Qian, Pei, Huang); Independent Researchers (Chen, Sun). Zhang's work done during an internship at Baidu. Mixed academia/industry; Baidu develops Ernie-5.0, one of the evaluated models

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Proposes an approach — benchmark RepoZero (repository generation from scratch reformulated as cross-language repository reproduction: 400 Py2JS and 200 C2Rust samples, output-equivalence black-box tests) with evaluation of 12 models under OpenHands-bash and 7 under Mini-SWE-Agent; and the Agentic Code-Test Evolution (ACE) test-time-scaling workflow, evaluated with DeepSeek V3.1

No SDD approach. ACE (Agentic Code-Test Evolution, authors' workflow, no version): coding agent generates the repository, testing agent generates test inputs and obtains ground truth by running the source repository, failures fed back for refinement (max retries 0/1/2). Scaffolds: OpenHands-bash and Mini-SWE-Agent (versions Not stated). Models: GLM-5, GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2.5, Kimi-K2.6, Ernie-5.0, Minimax-M2.5, Minimax-M2.7, DeepSeek V3.1, DeepSeek V3.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Claude-4.6-Sonnet

Per task (benchmark input, not an SDD artefact): functional specification of the source repository's APIs (the source entry/test file invoking the APIs, given in the prompt), four white-box test cases (inputs, ground-truth outputs, descriptions), constraints (target language only, no external packages/crates, same CLI arguments, byte-identical output, ESM .mjs files or Cargo project, project structure path, forbidden APIs). ACE: generated test-input JSON and failure messages

Benchmark run: agent reads the API specification and white-box cases -> generates the target repository with an entry point -> black-box tests compare outputs with the source repository. ACE: code generation -> testing agent generates inputs and runs the source repository for ground truth -> run generated repository -> if any case fails, error messages fed back and code refined ('do not rewrite from scratch') -> repeat until all pass or retry limit
None in the runs (autonomous). Human expert judgement only in manual selection of source repositories (determinism, open-source integrity, architectural complexity)
N/A (no SDD approach); agents generate whole repositories from an API specification; ACE exercised as a full loop with one model
Not classifiable; authors do not use SDD terms ('given only API specifications, an agent must re-implement an entire repository'; 'functional specifications of the source repository's APIs')
New project: repository generation from scratch, framed as cross-language reproduction (Python -> JavaScript/Node.js; C/C++ -> Rust)

600 samples (test files): Py2JS 400 (Easy 129, Medium 144, Hard 127), C2Rust 200 (Fig. 1: 60, 71, 69); each sample 1-20 API calls, about 40 test cases on average (20-60) after filtering from 60 generated; difficulty estimated by majority vote of Claude-4.6-Opus, GLM-5 and DeepSeek-V3.2 on LOC, API count and I/O complexity. Number of source repositories Not stated
Open-source libraries in five categories: Serialization & Data Formats, Cryptography & Encoding, Data Structures & Utilities, Mathematics & Science (e.g. mpmath), Specialized Tools
N/A (autonomous agents, no human participants)
Average token budget and average cost per sample in USD vs pass rate (Fig. 3, OpenHands-bash only; values in figure only)

Pass Rate (PR): sample passes only if outputs of source and target repositories are string-identical on all test cases; Success Rate (SR): fraction of test cases passed; reported as mean ± bootstrap standard deviation
None (architectural readability and structural integrity named as future work)
None
Pass rate by category; failure modes (no executable code, white-box case failure, runtime error, output mismatch in black-box tests); share of executable code with mismatched output (about 40%)

Automatic: generated repository executed in isolated Docker containers on hidden test inputs; outputs compared string-level with the source repository's stable outputs (each test case run 20 times during construction to discard non-deterministic ones); source test files read-only, hidden suite not exposed. Test cases generated by an LLM (model Not stated) and filtered

Criterion (sample level): PR = 1 only if all outputs match the source repository; no configuration-level threshold. Single run per configuration (no repetitions; bootstrap SD over samples); no cap on tool-calling iterations. Avg PR Py2JS / C2Rust (Easy/Medium/Hard in Tables 2-3). OpenHands-bash: (a) GLM-5 27.46 / 23.47; (b) GLM-5.1 34.19 / 35.05; (c) Kimi-K2.5 31.30 / 33.00; (d) Kimi-K2.6 33.25 / 38.51; (e) Ernie-5.0 19.46 / 13.97; (f) Minimax-M2.5 22.72 / 28.48; (g) Minimax-M2.7 27.15 / 32.12; (h) DeepSeek V3.1 26.08 / 32.49; (i) DeepSeek V3.2 29.01 / 33.55; (j) DeepSeek V4 Flash 30.74 / 35.41; (k) DeepSeek V4 Pro 39.78 / 35.53; (l) Claude-4.6-Sonnet 51.46 / 44.60. Mini-SWE-Agent: (m) GLM-5 45.52 / 38.51; (n) Kimi-K2.5 33.76 / 43.53; (o) Ernie-5.0 20.77 / 19.97; (p) Minimax-M2.5 30.63 / 25.39; (q) DeepSeek V3.1 43.76 / 39.45; (r) DeepSeek V3.2 44.20 / 37.41; (s) Claude-4.6-Sonnet 54.70 / 47.58. ACE with DeepSeek V3.1 on Py2JS, avg PR Retry-0 / Retry-1 / Retry-2: (t) OpenHands-bash + ACE 26.08 / 36.15 / 42.88; (u) Mini-SWE-Agent + ACE 43.76 / 45.67 / 52.06. Cost (Fig. 3) only graphically. For every configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors

Project/tasks: 600 RepoZero samples (Py2JS 400, C2Rust 200). Configurations: 12 models with OpenHands-bash, 7 with Mini-SWE-Agent; ACE vs no ACE (Retry-0) with DeepSeek V3.1 on both scaffolds. Baseline: Retry-0 (coding only) for ACE; none for the model comparison. Held constant: task prompts, white-box examples, constraints, Docker sandbox, hidden test suite; no iteration cap (only model output-token limits); agents allowed context-management and retrieval tools. Acceptance tests: hidden black-box output-equivalence tests against the source repository. Repetitions: none stated. Human intervention: none

Claude-4.6-Sonnet best (Py2JS 51.46 OpenHands, 54.70 Mini-SWE; C2Rust 44.60, 47.58); Ernie-5.0 lowest (13.97-20.77). Mini-SWE-Agent generally better than OpenHands-bash (e.g. GLM-5 Py2JS 45.52 vs 27.46), not for every pair (Minimax-M2.5 C2Rust 25.39 vs 28.48). Newer model versions in each family score higher under OpenHands-bash, with one exception under Mini-SWE-Agent (DeepSeek V3.1 above V3.2 on C2Rust, 39.45 vs 37.41). Pass rate roughly scales with cost, not monotonically (GLM-5.1 above GLM-5 at similar cost). ACE raises DeepSeek V3.1 Py2JS PR from 26.08 to 42.88 (OpenHands-bash) and from 43.76 to 52.06 (Mini-SWE-Agent) with two retries. About 40% of executable code fails output equivalence. No significance tests

Distinguished models and scaffolds (PR about 14-55%) and showed ACE gains; bootstrap SD about 2-3 points. Repeatability: single runs. Validity argued from consistent ordering within model families ('Benchmark2 principle'). Limitations stated by the authors: semi-synthetic benchmark 'precludes inherent quality guarantees'; proprietary models (GPT, Gemini) not evaluated with Mini-SWE-Agent due to cost; benchmark will leak once released (continuous updating proposed)

Limitations: semi-synthetic benchmark without inherent quality guarantees; limited Mini-SWE-Agent model coverage (no GPT/Gemini); future contamination. Gaps/future work: training paradigms (RL, distillation) for repository-level reasoning; metrics and constraints for architectural readability and structural integrity; larger, multilingual and industry-level scenarios; agents' self-verification and test synthesis; predictive oracle models when tests are scarce; long-context retention ('contextual drift')

Reporting inconsistencies: text says Claude-4.6-Sonnet 'consistently achieves the highest performance across all evaluation metrics' (p. 6), but other models are higher in several categories (Table 5, e.g. OpenHands Form GLM-5 58.09 vs 42.92) and in C2Rust SR (Table 6, DeepSeek V3.2 68.90 vs 68.04); 'successive iterations of the Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, and Minimax series exhibit progressive performance gains' (Tables 2 and 3, p. 7), but with Mini-SWE-Agent DeepSeek V3.1 is above V3.2 on C2Rust (39.45 vs 37.41, Table 3); Table 5 is captioned as pass rate but its category values exceed the overall pass rates of the same configurations in every category (e.g. OpenHands GLM-5 38.33-76.82 vs average 27.46), so it likely reports another metric; abstract gives 30-55% for the strongest agents while the conclusion says 'approximately 40%'; Table 7 Mini-SWE-Agent Retry-0 success rates (77.15, 67.07, 65.60) equal the C2Rust values of DeepSeek V3.1 in Table 6, although Table 7 is Py2JS; Table 6 scaffold not stated; appendix says GPT and Gemini were excluded from Mini-SWE-Agent, but they were not evaluated with OpenHands-bash either; C2Rust per-difficulty rates imply denominators of 60-61 (Easy) and 70 (Medium), not matching Fig. 1 counts; some Py2JS rates (e.g. Minimax-M2.5 Easy 29.97) are not multiples of 1/129. LLM used to generate tests and test cases not named. Baidu co-authors and Ernie-5.0 evaluated. Code: https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/RepoZero. No pre-registration. Programming languages: Python and C/C++ sources; JavaScript (Node.js) and Rust targets

Partly (0.5): low-performance and ACE-gain conclusions supported, but 'Claude highest across all metrics' is contradicted by Tables 5-6; benchmark validity rests on model-family ordering, which itself does not hold for DeepSeek V3.1 vs V3.2 with Mini-SWE-Agent on C2Rust (Table 3); and ACE conclusions rest on one model
Partly (0.5): brief limitations (semi-synthetic nature, Mini-SWE-Agent coverage, contamination) without a threats-to-validity discussion
Yes (1): NeurIPS 2026, Track on Evaluations and Datasets
Partly (0.5): authors created ACE (evaluated) and Baidu co-authors are the vendor of Ernie-5.0 (evaluated); the other models and scaffolds are independent

Partly (0.5): ACE uses standard coding agents and is feasible where an executable reference implementation exists (e.g. migration), but it needs the source repository as oracle, unavailable for new development, and its cost or compute is not reported
fields.why: ACE's requirements are only partly stated: it runs on standard coding agents (OpenHands-bash, Mini-SWE-Agent) with a testing agent, but its token, compute or money cost is not reported (Fig. 3 covers only the base OpenHands-bash runs), and it needs an executable source repository as oracle (p. 6, 8, 14). Partly is defensible; under the missing-information rule another reader could score No
fields.doubt: O artigo não reporta custo nem computação do ACE e este exige o repositório original como oráculo. Decide se fica Partly ou No pela regra de informação em falta.
